items.content:
Dal 6 ottobre Amazon apre la Festa delle Offerte Prime, 48 ore di sconti riservati agli abbonati Prime, e UGREEN concentra in questi due giorni i ribassi più alti della sua promozione d'autunno sui NAS NASync : sei modelli scontati sia su Amazon sia sul sito del produttore.

Un NAS (Network Attached Storage) collega al router uno o più hard disk e li rende raggiungibili da telefoni, computer e televisori, sia sulla rete di casa sia da fuori tramite Internet.

Il secondo argomento riguarda il controllo dei dati, poiché foto, documenti e backup restano sui dischi di casa e non passano dai server di terzi.

Per tutti i NASync è presente la cifratura delle connessioni con TLS/SSL, RSA e AES , l'autenticazione a due fattori e un Security Manager che controlla il sistema in modo continuo. I NAS hanno ottenuto anche la certificazione di sicurezza ETSI EN 303 645, rilasciata da TÜV SÜD, e quella statunitense TRUSTe. Anche il riconoscimento dei volti e degli oggetti nell'app Foto gira sul NAS senza inviare le immagini a servizi esterni.

C'è poi la velocità. Dentro casa i trasferimenti dipendono dalla rete locale e non dalla linea internet in upload, che nelle connessioni domestiche resta di solito il collo di bottiglia, specialmente se non si ha una fibra seria. Su una porta a 2,5 Gb/s si arriva a un massimo teorico di 312,5 MB/s, che vuol dire copiare un video 4K da 20 GB in poco più di un minuto.

È facile anche la configurazione, che sui NAS UGREEN richiede meno di dieci minuti e un'unica app per gestire file, backup delle foto e streaming verso la TV.

La prima decisione riguarda il numero di alloggiamenti per i dischi . Con due dischi si può impostare il RAID 1, che scrive gli stessi dati su entrambi: se un disco si guasta, i file restano sull'altro, ma la capienza utile è alla fine quella di un solo disco perché il secondo serve come sicurezza. Con quattro o sei alloggiamenti si possono usare il RAID 5 e il RAID 6, che salvano su tutti i dischi anche delle informazioni di controllo; quindi se un disco si rompe (due, con il RAID 6), il NAS ricostruisce i file mancanti a partire da quelli rimasti.

Conviene pensare a quanto crescerà l'archivio nei prossimi anni, perché quando tutti gli alloggiamenti saranno occupati, per avere più spazio bisognerà sostituire i dischi con altri più capienti, uno alla volta, oppure collegare un'unità esterna. Partire con un NAS a quattro alloggiamenti e due soli dischi lascia invece margine per aggiungerne altri due in seguito.

La seconda riguarda il processore. I modelli della serie DH di UGREEN usano chip ARM di Rockchip, poco energivori e sufficienti per archivio, backup e streaming , con una versione semplificata del sistema operativo UGOS Pro e memoria non espandibile.

La serie DXP monta processori Intel, ha la versione completa di UGOS Pro, memoria espandibile e due slot M.2 per SSD da usare come cache o come spazio aggiuntivo. È quindi la strada per chi vuole affiancare all'archivio carichi più pesanti , come le macchine virtuali o un server multimediale che converte i video al volo, oppure servire molti utenti insieme.

La terza e ultima scelta è quella della rete . Una porta da 1 Gb/s basta per foto e documenti, quella da 2,5 Gb/s è utile con i video pesanti, mentre i 10 Gb/s servono a chi lavora in rete su file di grandi dimensioni e ha computer e switch in grado di sfruttarli.

Il DH2300 è pensato per chi un NAS non l'ha mai avuto e vuole soprattutto mettere al sicuro le foto di famiglia, smettendo di rincorrere lo spazio libero sul telefono. Ha due alloggiamenti: con due dischi in RAID 1 ogni file viene salvato due volte e, se uno dei dischi si guasta, l'archivio resta intatto. Si configura dall'app UGREEN con una procedura guidata e, per collegare lo smartphone, basta avvicinarlo al NAS grazie all'NFC .

Collegato al televisore del salotto tramite l'uscita HDMI 4K, riproduce film e video di casa senza bisogno di un computer . Il processore Rockchip a otto core e i 4 GB di memoria bastano per archivio, backup e streaming, con una capienza che arriva a 64 TB complessivi.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il DH2300, da listino di 246,99 euro, scende a 189,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Quando i dispositivi da salvare diventano tanti, tra gli smartphone di tutta la famiglia, i portatili e magari il lavoro da casa, due dischi si riempiono in fretta. Il DH4300 Plus raddoppia gli alloggiamenti, fino a 128 TB, e permette di scegliere il RAID 5 o il RAID 6 , che proteggono i dati sacrificando meno spazio.

La porta di rete a 2,5 Gb/s accorcia i tempi quando si salvano video pesanti, e il processore Rockchip RK3588C con 8 GB di memoria regge più persone collegate insieme. Chi ha un po' di dimestichezza può installare applicazioni aggiuntive tramite Docker , mentre per tutti gli altri restano la configurazione guidata e l'app unica del DH2300.

Nei giorni della Festa delle Offerte Prime, e fino all'11 ottobre, il prezzo scende da 439,99 euro a 319,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP4800 Plus è il modello per chi dal NAS vuole qualcosa in più di un archivio , quindi un server multimediale che converte i video al volo, qualche macchina virtuale, i backup automatici di tutti i computer di casa o dello studio.

Il processore Intel Pentium Gold a cinque core lavora con 8 GB di memoria DDR5, espandibili fino a 64 GB, e il sistema gira su un SSD dedicato da 128 GB.

Accanto ai quattro alloggiamenti per hard disk ci sono due slot per SSD M.2 , da usare come cache per velocizzare i file aperti più spesso con una capienza massima di 144 TB.

La porta da 10 Gb/s, affiancata da una seconda a 2,5 Gb/s, serve a chi lavora su file grandi da un computer collegato via cavo, e il lettore di schede SD permette di scaricare le foto della fotocamera direttamente sul NAS.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il prezzo scende da 729,99 euro a 549,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Con sei alloggiamenti per hard disk e due per SSD, il DXP6800 Pro si rivolge a un piccolo studio professionale o a chi custodisce un archivio video di anni perché può arrivare fino a 208 TB di spazio.

Il processore Intel Core i5 a dieci core permette a più persone di lavorare contemporaneamente sugli stessi file, anche mentre il NAS esegue i backup o converte un video.

Le due porte di rete da 10 Gb/s si possono unire fino a 20 Gb/s , e le due Thunderbolt 4 servono a collegare dischi esterni veloci, per esempio per scaricare il materiale di una giornata di riprese. L 'uscita HDMI arriva fino all'8K.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il DXP6800 Pro è in offerta, passando dal listino di 1.209,99 euro a 899,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP2800 è per chi si accontenta di due dischi ma dal NAS vuole più di un archivio di foto. Ha gli stessi due alloggiamenti del DH2300, ma monta un processore Intel più potente e la versione completa del sistema UGOS Pro , con più applicazioni a disposizione. La memoria si può ampliare fino a 16 GB e due slot per SSD servono a velocizzare i file usati più spesso.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre si scende dal listino di 439,99 euro a 329,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP480T Plus rinuncia agli hard disk e accoglie quattro SSD M.2 NVMe , così da lavorare sui file video direttamente dalla rete senza rallentamenti. Monta lo stesso Core i5 del DXP6800 Pro, una porta da 10 Gb/s e due Thunderbolt 4.

In questo caso lo sconto vale solo il 6 e 7 ottobre: in quei due giorni il prezzo di listino di 999,99 euro passa a 749,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Con la Festa delle Offerte Prime è il momento giusto per smettere di pagare lo spazio online ogni mese e riportare a casa i propri ricordi, una volta per tutte.

Sui NAS UGREEN i prezzi della festa restano validi dal 6 fino all'11 ottobre su tutti i modelli tranne il DXP480T Plus, che sale dal prezzo scontato di 749,99 euro a 899,99 euro già dall'8 ottobre. Tutte le offerte sono sulla pagina UGREEN di Amazon e sulla pagina dedicata del sito UGREEN .
items.author: Sergio Donato

items.title: Questions remain over Ebola patient who travelled across three nations undetected
items.summary: Fresh details reveal how the 40-year-old businessman flew and crossed regional borders while seriously ill.
items.content:
A Kenyan businessman was able to spend time in one of the regions worst-affected by Ebola, then travel to two more countries before his illness was identified.

The 40-year-old - who was only diagnosed with the deadly infectious disease after arriving seriously ill at a Nairobi hospital - became Kenya's first confirmed case. He died two days later on 5 October.

That his infection went undetected at multiple health facilities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and two airport health screenings in Uganda and Kenya has raised serious questions about these nations' biosecurity during a significant outbreak.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.

Africa CDC, the continent's leading public health agency, has now reconstructed the Kenyan patient's movements across nearly six weeks, revealing several missed opportunities to detect his infection and potentially preventing dozens of people from coming into contact with the deadly virus.

The account, presented by the agency's emergency director, Dr Wessam Mankoula, provides the clearest picture yet of how the businessman travelled thousands of kilometres while growing increasingly unwell.

The man, whose identity has not been made public, had lived in DR Congo for seven years and had travelled across three of its provinces on business.

Exactly when or where he contracted Ebola remains unclear - but it was present in all three provinces he went through by early October, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

The man had spent much of late August and early September in the province of Bas-Uélé, visiting towns including Buta, Aketi and Likati.

The WHO confirmed an Ebola case in Buta in August, prior to his visit, though there is no evidence he contracted the virus there.

His symptoms first emerged around 15 September. He was given antibiotics and sent home.

Two days later, he was admitted to the Tongo Etandi Health Centre in Bondo, where he remained until 19 September.

Despite suffering from fever and a rash, he was diagnosed with a skin infection.

Without an Ebola test being taken at any point during his travels, it is hard to say exactly when he contracted the virus. Those symptoms are consistent with the early stages of the disease, but also other infections common to the region, such as malaria.

On 20 September, he flew to Kisangani, a city with a population of about 1.5 million people on the Congo River, where he spent more than 10 days seeking medical care.

We do not know which hospitals or clinics treated him there, nor what medications they gave him. Kisangani is the capital of Tshopo province which has only recorded 51 Ebola cases.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

Why Uganda is winning the battle against Ebola as virus spreads in DR Congo

However, on 1 October, more than two weeks after first becoming ill, the businessman boarded another domestic flight to Beni, before continuing his journey to Kasindi, a busy border town.

Both Beni and Kasindi are in North Kivu, which has recorded 1,755 Ebola infections and more than 1,000 deaths, making it one of the Congolese provinces worst-hit by the disease.

But he did not stay there long, crossing into Uganda later that day.

Uganda imposed restrictions on movement across its border with DR Congo shortly after the outbreak began in May.

The country has experience containing several Ebola outbreaks, including through surveillance, contact tracing and the isolation of suspected cases. It has had some cases this year - mostly among people travelling from DR Congo - but was declared free of the disease in August.

But the border between the two nations stretches for hundreds of kilometres through remote terrain, making it difficult to police.

It remains unclear whether the businessman passed through an official health checkpoint when he crossed the border.

Once he had, he travelled by road to the capital, Kampala, and then Entebbe International Airport, where he boarded a flight to Nairobi on 3 October.

Ugandan officials said his temperature was normal when he passed through airport screening. Health experts say his case highlights the limitations of relying on temperature checks and self-declarations.

Mankoula said investigators were examining whether the man's medication could have suppressed his temperature. He may have also not had a fever when he passed through the checks.

Similarly, he was not flagged as a suspected Ebola patient when he reached Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, where a relative collected him and drove him directly to Nairobi Hospital, a private medical facility in the Kenyan capital.

By then, he was suffering from fever, chills, muscle pain, a sore throat and bleeding.

Laboratory tests confirmed that he had contracted the Bundibugyo species of Ebola - the same one responsible for the outbreak in DR Congo.

He was placed in isolation while his condition deteriorated. He died on 5 October and was buried the following day under strict infection-control measures.

The Kenyan government says it has now identified 66 people who may have been in contact with him after he arrived there. The WHO says the number is likely to rise as contact-tracing in Uganda and DR Congo continues.

The quarantine arrangements have also raised concerns among some healthcare workers, amid questions about how the patient was handled at Nairobi Hospital.

Kenya's health ministry says more than 652,000 travellers have been screened and nearly 5,000 healthcare workers trained to deal with Ebola, with five facilities designated to handle cases.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person who has developed symptoms, or through contaminated materials.

Its incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning someone exposed to the virus may not become ill until several weeks later.

Mankoula urged travellers experiencing symptoms of Ebola to report them, saying early medical attention could improve their chances of survival.

"When you reveal any Ebola-related symptoms early, you're not only preventing the virus spreading to other countries but you're also protecting yourself first," he said.

The WHO has warned that stigma surrounding Ebola could discourage people from reporting symptoms or seeking medical care, potentially allowing the virus to spread undetected.

The agency says it is stepping up efforts to encourage this by reducing fear and misinformation about the disease - something that is a big problem in DR Congo, where some health workers have been attacked by people who claim Ebola doesn't exist.

Recovery of Ebola patients offers rare moments of joy at epicentre of outbreak

'They said it isn't real': Ebola rumours fuel attacks on health workers

items.title: 'Everyone hates the police' – what France's school protests reveal about a divided nation
items.summary: Students taking to the streets have become a focal point in the country's increasingly polarised politics.
items.content:
As dustbins burn and students chant "everyone hates the police" in the French city of Lille, one teenager explains why he and his friends have taken to the streets.

"There aren't even enough chairs. We have to go and find some at the start of every lesson," the 16-year-old, who did not want to give his name, says of his school.

"We've got 50 minutes to eat at lunchtime but there are 2,000 of us that need to get through the canteen."

He is one of hundreds of thousands of students who have protested across France since the end of last month over staff shortages and dilapidated facilities in the country's lycées, secondary schools attended by 15 to 18-year-olds.

Despite the government's apparent attempts to make concessions, the students show no sign of backing down.

"They have armies, they have the police, they have the powers," says Massicella, 18, as she marches through Lille. "But we have the mass population."

The protests, which have turned violent, have become a focal point in France's polarised politics, with all sides accusing the other of escalating tensions. As a presidential election approaches, politicians on both the hard right and hard left have sought to capitalise on the unrest and on what many see as the government's inability to resolve the crisis.

The protests - ignited at the Lycée Antoine-de-Saint-Exupéry in the deprived Paris suburb of Créteil - have struck a chord across the country.

Videos of rats scuttling through corridors in other lycées soon hit social media, providing striking symbols of the discontent. Other videos on TikTok and Instagram showed broken toilets, holes in walls and mouldy ceilings across the country. Students have complained of unbearable heat in the summer and freezing classrooms in the winter.

The anger has also focused on long school hours, chronic staff shortages, overcrowded classes and a deeply unpopular university admissions system.

The problem for the French government - which became clearer as we spoke to dozens of pupils this week - is that even if a tiny minority of schools have a problem with rodents, a very large number of pupils believe their own education is failing them.

On Tuesday, the government said 250,000 people marched, most of them young. The trade unions said it was more like half a million.

But it is not just students taking to the streets - their teachers are joining them.

Secondary school teacher Marine Monins, who joined the demonstrations in Lille, shows us a laminated timetable which she says illustrates the problem.

It has become normal for pupils to start at 8am and finish as late as 6pm, but the days are punctuated by hours-long gaps because of bad planning and staff shortages.

When lessons do go ahead, the classes are typically packed with 35 pupils (by comparison, the average secondary school class in England has fewer than 23 pupils).

"It's now impossible to give every child the attention they deserve," Monins explains.

On Thursday, the French government made its first sign of ceding ground to protesters, with a promise of 3,000 extra supply teachers in the coming days.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has said by the end of October there will be a plan unveiled to respond to the crisis. Ministers have said they could look again at resources for schools within next year's squeezed budget.

But this has been met with a collective shrug at barricaded school gates across the country.

"It goes beyond having decent toilets in schools," lycée student Alcidor says in Paris, under the statue of Marianne at Place de la République, a place synonymous with protest.

"It's strong anger from the youth in France that doesn't feel represented, that feels abandoned, that feels unheard and is scared of what's coming in the future."

So far, almost 7,000 people have been detained during the disorder with more than 85% being children, according to the interior ministry.

More than 700 police officers have been injured in the past three weeks.

But rights groups and unions accuse the police of resorting to heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flash-ball guns. At least 200 pupils have been injured, along with dozens of teachers.

A 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off during a confrontation between police and demonstrators in the northern city of Lens.

Reports of how the teenager sustained the injury differ. A police union source cited by the AFP news agency said the boy appeared to have picked up a sting-ball grenade fired by riot police, which then exploded in his hand. However, a witness told local media that the teenager did not pick up the grenade.

A teacher at the boy's school, Bastien Riez, who is also a union rep, believes that current police tactics could irrevocably damage the relationship with France's youth.

"For many, this is their first experience of democracy and protest, and they are met with police and a sham of social dialogue and democracy. I fear that many young people will stop believing in this so-called democracy altogether."

Police have since been banned from using stun grenades at school protests.

But Parisian pupil Kaspar, 15, speaks of his fear when coming face-to-face with police in full riot gear. He says he and his friends have been protesting peacefully, but strangers were hijacking their protests.

"These people are coming just to shoot fireworks at police officers and they run. This is not the message we want to send to the world."

Police chiefs say violence, directed by agitators who have no link to the schools, is making their job incredibly hard.

Michel Chaballier, deputy secretary-general of the National Police Commissioners' Union (SCPN), says he fears the "political climate has been radicalised", and it was more and more difficult to have a calm, constructive public debate ahead of the national vote next spring.

"Police officers find themselves caught in the middle of this social tension, which is sometimes fuelled by irresponsible politicians," he says. "That's a shame, because I think this country deserves better."

The protests have become another bruising battleground in France's culture wars, with leaders of the hard left and right seeking to capitalise.

More than three-quarters of under-30s in France interviewed for an Ipsos survey conducted for Aix-Marseille University this week said they were worried about the state of their country.

But many people have a more profound and wider concern about just how dramatically the middle ground in France is eroding, leaving a chasm in the political landscape.

The education crisis is symptomatic of this but also threatens to act as an accelerant.

Most polling suggests more and more French citizens are looking to political extremes for answers to their problems – whether they are linked to education, the economy, identity or immigration.

Marine Le Pen of the hard right National Rally is the frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race.

Next, neck and neck, are Édouard Philippe and Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

Philippe was a prime minister in President Emmanuel Macron's first term and has since founded a centre-right party called Horizons.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a veteran hard-left politician and founder of France Unbowed (LFI), has been a prominent older face among the students at rallies over the past three weeks.

Opponents have accused him of provoking and profiting from the unrest, while he counters that only his party truly represents the French youth.

He claims the current movement that has emerged from the schools protest is the most potent since 1968, when huge demonstrations almost brought down the government of President Charles de Gaulle. At its height, 10 million workers were on the streets before fresh elections led to the revolt fizzling out, but not before carving an indelible memory in French social history.

Despite being born more than four decades later, an exasperated generation of French teenagers are looking to the past for inspiration.

"I personally want to reproduce 1968!" Massicella declares in Lille, as she nears the end of the protest march.

Le Pen has stayed away from the protests and her most notable interventions have come in condemning the damage to schools, which is said to run into the millions of euros.

She has also suggested that parents of children who have committed the vandalism should pay for repairs.

The principle of casseur-payeur – those who break have to pay – has been an impassioned topic that has dominated French media this week.

The problem for President Macron is that there is no quick fix.

This is not a scenario where there is an unpopular piece of legislation that can be withdrawn in a hasty reverse ferret the prime minister is tasked with performing. That was the case with the gilets jaunes – the relentless protest in high vis jackets over a fuel tax rise nearly a decade ago.

Wholesale reform of the education system would cost billions – in new classrooms, new facilities, new teachers – and take years to achieve.

And changes that may seem more easily done – such as a reduction of the length of the school day – would be hugely problematic to implement logistically.

items.title: Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices
items.summary: The US president hopes to ease his party's pain before next month's midterm elections, writes the BBC's North America correspondent.
items.content:
Donald Trump's decision to import Russian fuel to the US represents a remarkable about-face from the president.

Just three weeks ago, Trump signed legislation to authorise fresh American sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas.

Now, Trump says, Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel to the US and world markets in the coming months.

The deal comes as Trump is still grappling with the political fallout of the Iran war and its impact on global energy prices, weeks before American voters head to the polls in the midterm elections.

As the cost of fuel has skyrocketed in America, his standing with the public – stung by the higher prices at the pump and knock-on effects that led to across-the board inflation – has soured.

The toll the war is taking has been acutely felt by US agricultural states, which rely heavily on diesel to operate farming machinery and to transport their products to market.

It is these states – places like Iowa, Kansas, Texas and Ohio – that have become unexpected political battlegrounds in the upcoming elections that will determine if Republicans maintain control of Congress.

Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky criticises 'gift to Putin'

For months, the American president has been searching for ways to ease his party's political pain.

He recently pressured European allies to further tap their oil reserves . He deferred federal taxes on the fuel and authorised supplies designated for farm use to be used in interstate trucking.

He has also promised that he would not renew attacks on Iran until after the midterms – an unusually frank acknowledgement of the political impact the ongoing conflict is having.

His decision to strike a deal with Russia's Putin is only the latest, most dramatic effort.

Trump's Truth Social posts often provide incomplete information, of course. The details of exactly how Russia is supplying this fuel to the global market, and what they might get for in return – besides much-needed hard currency – is unclear.

It opens Trump to criticism from European allies and American politicians that his administration is now helping to fund the Russian war machine.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the deal a "gift" to Putin that Russia would "repay" with "terror and perfidy".

"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on X.

It is also uncertain exactly how much Trump's move will help Republicans at the ballot box.

The promised European diesel release hasn't moved energy prices significantly, and there's no information on the speed with which Russian fuel could enter the market.

Its diesel refinery capacity has been damaged by repeated Ukrainian strikes – attacks that Trump has encouraged Zelensky to curtail.

The US uses approximately 3.6 million barrels of diesel a day, so even if Russia delivers its promised 300,000 tons this month, that amounts to approximately half of the US daily consumption.

With less than a month before November's midterm elections, early voting has already started in many states. The political cake, as the saying goes, is all but baked.

"Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump wrote in his Truth Social post.

But over the past seven months, prices on energy, fuel and consumer goods have only gone up - even as Trump and his officials have repeatedly assured an uneasy public a successful resolution to the war, and an easing of its economic impact, is nearly at hand.

Trump may be left hoping that his latest deal, setting aside its potentially uncomfortable diplomatic issues, will be enough to convince American voters that his promise of impending economic relief is more than just empty words.

Trump wants to reduce the cost of fuel as the midterms loom - will it work?

items.title: Three men found guilty of murdering Australian brothers and US friend in Mexico
items.summary: Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend Carter Rhoad were on a surf trip when they were killed in an apparent botched robbery.
items.content:
Three men have been found guilty of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, and their US friend Carter Rhoad during a surfing trip in Mexico in 2024.

The men's full names could not be given for legal reasons, and they were only identified as Jesús Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús. They are yet to be sentenced - but are likely to spend the rest of their lives in a prison.

Debra Robinson, the brothers' mother, told the courtroom that her sons' murders had taken "the future we had imagined with them".

During the trial in the northern Baja California state, the court heard that the tourists were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck in a secluded beach area.

Their bodies were later found dumped down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads.

The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the coastal area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico.

Robinson and her husband Martin have been at the court in the coastal town of Ensenada throughout the trial, and delivered emotional testimony during closing arguments before Friday's verdict.

"It's hard for a parent to lose a son, and we lost two sons," Martin said.

Family members of Carter Rhoad joined the trial by video link.

Robinson told reporters outside court a week ago that the couple were "deeply grateful" to Australians for the outpouring of support they had received and that they "feel the love and their arms around us".

During the month-long trial, the prosecution had sought 150 years in prison for each of the three defendants.

In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, Jesús Gerardo (alias "El Kekas"), was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery.

At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings.

The beach town has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers, but the chilling murders revealed how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico.

The only explanation the authorities were able to give was that the surfers - all in their early 30s - had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Their killings happened barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week, when their families were able to identify them.

At the time, the surfer community in Ensenada turned out in force to honour the men by paddling out at a popular surfing spot and throwing flowers into the sea.

Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

Amid the demands for action, state Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila tried to ease public fears about the widespread violence.

"Baja California is and will continue to be a state with safe tourism for the thousands of people who visit us from the rest of the country and the world," she said.

"I send my condolences and solidarity to the families at this difficult time."

Trial over killing of Australian surfer brothers and US friend starts in Mexico

items.title: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he would not watch it
items.summary: The planned execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.
items.content:
JD Vance has cast doubt on the Pentagon's plans to livestream a firing squad execution.

The US vice-president expressed uncertainty to reporters about whether the December execution would go ahead as planned, saying: "I don't know that that's actually going to happen". He added that "if it's through livestream, I'm not going to be watching it".

Hours later, US President Donald Trump said he "absolutely" approved of the livestream plan but said the Pentagon was still "making a determination" on it.

Nidal Hasan killed 13 unarmed soldiers at the Fort Hood military base in Texas in 2009 and injured another 32. His execution would be the first military firing squad execution in more than 60 years.

The Pentagon announced its desire to execute the former US Army major by firing squad over the attack on 3 December earlier this week.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth then said the execution would be livestreamed for the public, as "people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things".

Trump was asked about the possibility that visuals of Hasan's execution could be used as propaganda for terrorists as he left the White House on Friday.

Calling Hasan "totally nuts", he replied: "I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes, and I think that the death penalty is a very worthy way of going for him."

The Pentagon declined to comment further when asked for more information about a decision on the livestream.

Vance condemned Hasan's attack on the base as "the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11" while speaking to reporters on Friday.

Asked about how his Catholic faith affected his stance on the plan to stream a public execution, Vance questioned whether it would happen.

But he noted that Hasan, a military psychiatrist, was meant to treat soldiers for mental illness and other problems, but had instead "took them at their most vulnerable and gunned down these people where they lived".

The possible livestreaming of the execution has been met with criticism from both political parties.

Republican Senator John Curtis pointed to Rome's history of a "bloody spectacle" corrupting people who watched, warning that public executions eroded civilisations "when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment".

Curtis said that Hegseth's plan "risks feeding that appetite" and urged him to reconsider.

"The victims deserve justice administered with solemnity. Broadcasting a death diminishes us and is not an effective deterrent."

Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group.

Georgia lawmaker Austin Scott, a Republican, said that while he "absolutely" supported the death sentence, livestreaming executions was "what jihadists do - America is better than that".

John Bolton, a former national security adviser during the first Trump administration, told BBC's Radio 4 PM that he supported capital punishment, but that the livestream was "unnecessary" because there were provisions for interested parties to view the execution in person.

"I just think this is a mark by Secretary Hegseth doing something he thinks will please President Trump," he said. "I think that's really not appropriate for a secretary of defence."

The US Conference of Catholic Bishops also condemned the decision to publicly livestream Hasan's execution, expressing "shock and great sorrow".

The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".

Hasan opened fire in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines on 5 November 2009.

He later admitted in court that he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes". He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military.

It was the deadliest ever non-combat attack on a US military base.

While there were more than 2,700 executions across 17 countries last year, only two nations carried them out publicly. Eleven public executions were known to have been carried out in Iran in 2025 and another six in Afghanistan, according to Amnesty International.

When Hegseth told reporters on Thursday about his livestreaming plans, he did not specify where or how the execution would be shown.

A Pentagon spokesperson later reiterated to the BBC that Hasan's execution "will be livestreamed" but said the government had no further details.

The White House did not respond to an inquiry about whether it expected to show Hasan's planned execution on its social media channels.

Fort Hood survivor supports gunman's execution by firing squad but questions livestream

All of the social media platforms the US government has accounts on have prohibitions in place on violent images and videos, as well as those that show death or glorify or make a spectacle of violence.

Meta - owner of Instagram, Facebook and Threads - explicitly bans any livestream of capital punishment.

YouTube bans all "violent or gory content intended to shock or disgust viewers", while TikTok similarly bars "extremely graphic, violent or disturbing content" that includes the "moment of someone's death" and "the shooting of an individual".

But both YouTube and TikTok make exceptions in instances of "public interest".

Asked whether a livestream of an execution qualifies for the exception if it is government-sanctioned, a TikTok spokeswoman said: "Regardless, I'd point you back to the not allowed section which reflects our approach."

The policy at X, which has loosened content moderation since billionaire Elon Musk took over the platform, prohibits content "glorifying" violence.

Meta, YouTube and X did not respond to multiple BBC requests for comment.

items.title: RTX Spark, modelli, prezzi e disponibilità in Italia. Per Surface Laptop Ultra ci sarà da attendere
items.summary: I primi notebook con NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X si possono già configurare e ordinare in Italia: per la nuova piattaforma NVIDIA si parte da poco più di 3.000 euro e si arriva a oltre 6.000, con la differenza di prezzo legata quasi esclusivamente alla memoria. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Sono aperti da meno di 24 ore i preordini dei primi laptop con piattaforma RTX Spark, e già arrivano le prime indicazioni: in Germania e in Francia, dove il Surface Laptop Ultra viene venduto, la versione da 128 GB di RAM è andata sold out in poche ore. Non possiamo ovviamente sapere di quanti laptop stiamo parlando, ma è evidente che da anni chi usa Windows aspettava una workstation con le caratteristiche promesse dal nuovo chip NVIDIA: consumi ridotti, piena potenza anche a batteria, fino a 128 GB di memoria unificata e prestazioni allineate a quelle della RTX 5070.

Il Surface Laptop Ultra in Italia al momento non arriva, e non escludiamo che la scelta possa essere legata proprio alla poca disponibilità di prodotto, ma MSI, Asus e Lenovo hanno aperto i preordini per i loro modelli, e la buona notizia è che si partirà da circa 3.000 euro, grazie a Lenovo, che offre una configurazione base molto allettante.

Lo Yoga Pro 9n Gen 11 da 15" parte infatti da 3.019,01 euro con N1X a 18 core (P-core fino a 3,90 GHz), 32 GB di LPDDR5X-9400 e 512 GB di storage. Se si vuole 1 TB di storage servono 90 euro in più.

Per avere più memoria bisogna passare alla versione da 20 core, con P-core fino a 4,00 GHz, che parte però da 4.839 euro con 64 GB di RAM e 1 TB di disco. Il disco da 2 TB costa 520 euro in più, si arriva a 5.339 euro. Stranamente basso il prezzo chiesto per passare alla versione da 128 GB: solo 300 euro, per un totale di 5.659 euro. È un prezzo alto, ma è anche il più basso in assoluto al quale si può trovare un RTX Spark con 128 GB di RAM.

Lenovo non ha solo il 15": c'è anche lo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 Gen 11 da 16", convertibile con OLED 2,8K (2.880 x 1.800) touch a 120 Hz e penna. Qui si parte da 3.619,01 euro per la versione con processore a 18 core, 32 GB di RAM e SSD da 512 GB. L'SSD da 1 TB costa qui 80 euro in più, mentre per il 20 core si passa a 4.759 euro, perché oltre al processore cambia anche la memoria, che sale a 64 GB. Il disco è da 1 TB, con 500 euro in più per il 2 TB. La memoria, invece, non si può espandere: questa macchina viene venduta solo nei tagli da 32 GB o da 64 GB.

MSI propone solo laptop con processore completo, quindi CPU a 20 core e GPU a 6.144 core. Il Prestige N16 Flip AI+, convertibile da 16" con batteria da 99,9 Wh e display Tandem OLED 3840 x 2400, parte da 4.299 euro per la versione da 64 GB con disco da 1 TB e arriva a 6.399 euro per quella da 128 GB con disco da 2 TB.

ASUS è l'unica a offrire RTX Spark in formato compatto, con il ProArt P14: 14" OLED 3K a 120 Hz, 1,48 kg e batteria da 90 Wh. I due modelli disponibili sono posizionati a 3.599 euro con 32 GB e a 5.599 euro con 128 GB, entrambi con la versione del processore più potente e con disco da 1 TB. C'è anche il modello da 16": 4.599 euro per 64 GB e 1 TB, 6.399 euro per il 128 GB con 2 TB.

Microsoft ha il bellissimo Surface Laptop Ultra, che possiamo considerare il reference design della piattaforma. In Italia non arriverà subito, ma possiamo prendere come riferimento i prezzi di Francia e Germania: 2.899 euro per RTX Spark in versione 18 core con GPU da 5.120 core, 24 GB e SSD da 512 GB; 3.399 euro per quella da 24 GB e 1 TB; 3.759 euro per 32 GB e 1 TB. La variante con processore completo, a 20 core e con GPU da 6.144 core, parte da 4.239 euro (32 GB, 1 TB), sale a 4.959 euro con 64 GB e a 5.439 euro con 2 TB, fino a 6.879 euro per la versione da 128 GB, che risulta, come abbiamo detto, già esaurita.

Al momento Dell e HP, gli altri due partner di NVIDIA per il lancio, non hanno annunciato la disponibilità per il nostro mercato.

items.title: Thai Queen makes first solo flight in fighter jet
items.summary: Thailand’s Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.
items.content:
Thailand's Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.

The Queen was shown boarding a Gripen on 8 October at an airfield in Surat Thani province, southern Thailand, while King Maha Vajiralongkorn watched from the ground.

The Royal Household has said she is an experienced pilot, having logged about 1,188 hours across several types of aircraft since she began flying in 2010.

She also co-piloted aircraft carrying the King on official visits to other countries, the Royal Household said.

items.title: Deterministic Simulation Testing in Celld
items.summary: Article URL: https://celld.dev/docs/engineering/deterministic-simulation-testing/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50024805 Points: 8 # Comments: 0
items.content:
We are building celld , a runtime for Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects applications on your own machines. It can run with an S3-compatible object store as its only external service dependency.

celld is a distributed system. Making distributed systems reliable is hard, partly because we can unintentionally rely on assumptions that don’t hold in practice, even when we know the pitfalls. Peter Deutsch’s The Eight Fallacies of Distributed Computing lists eight such assumptions, including “The network is reliable” and “Latency is zero.”

A bug can depend on a particular sequence of delayed messages, failed writes, and node restarts. Those events can happen in a different order on the next test run, making the failure difficult to reproduce. We need to be able to repeat the failing run so we can investigate the cause and check whether a proposed fix really resolves the problem.

That is why we use deterministic simulation testing (DST) . Our simulator is still under development and is not included in celld’s public repository, but it has already found previously unknown bugs. In this article, we’ll walk through how DST works in celld and how it helped us find, reproduce, and fix one of those bugs.

DST runs celld’s production code in an environment controlled by a simulator.

A cell in celld runs application code and has its own SQLite database. As cells do their work, celld handles events such as incoming requests, completed storage operations, and timer firings. The code that selects the next event is separate from the code that handles it. This lets the simulator control the order of events while running the same event-handling code as in production .

The simulator also controls when asynchronous tasks run and how object storage responds. It can delay a write or make it fail. It can advance simulated time without waiting for real time to pass. We use this control to test how time-dependent behavior, such as retries and alarms, interacts with other events.

We configure which requests and faults the simulator can explore. Within those limits, it uses random choices to generate requests, select what runs next, decide whether storage operations succeed or fail, and choose which faults occur and when.

A seed is the starting value for its random-number generator. With the same code, settings, and seed, we get the same sequence, intermediate states, and result. We can explore different runs by changing the seed, then repeat a failing run to trace where things went wrong.

After each action, a checker uses observed responses and stored data to test invariants : conditions we define that the system must uphold throughout a run. The test initializes celld with the simulated environment, then explores actions up to a configured limit. In pseudocode:

Here, an action is something the simulator can advance: delivering a request, letting a task run, advancing the simulated clock, or completing a storage operation. If no actions are available, the test checks its completion conditions, such as whether all planned requests have finished.

The simplified replay below starts after Cell A has inserted a row into SQLite. Watch how the data is saved to object storage before celld receives confirmation. Other requests or background tasks can run in that gap, while celld is still waiting to return success to the client. Bugs can emerge when these operations interleave in unexpected ways. The simulator controls these steps separately so we can explore different execution orders and replay those that expose a bug.

Press Next to step through choosing an action, animating it, and revealing its result.

The replay above shows a successful request. Next, we’ll look at an execution order that exposed a bug in celld.

An alarm schedules a cell to run application code at a specified time. The cell need not stay in memory until then: celld can unload an idle cell to make room for others and load it again in time to run its alarm.

The alarm's scheduled time is stored in the cell's SQLite database . If the cell has been unloaded, finding its alarm from SQLite alone would mean opening its database again. Doing that for every cell would be expensive, so celld instead scans wake entries in object storage. Each entry identifies a cell and when to reactivate it. Once the cell is active, celld reads the scheduled time from SQLite to determine when to run the alarm.

When we found this bug, celld reused wake entries to reduce the number of writes to object storage. For example, an application could delete a 10:00 alarm and then set a new one for 10:05. If the 10:00 wake entry was still present, celld could reuse it to reactivate the cell at 10:00, early enough for the new alarm. Once the cell was active, celld would read 10:05 from SQLite and wait until then to run the alarm. 1

Deleting the 10:00 alarm clears its scheduled time from SQLite. Once that change has been saved to object storage, celld returns success to the client. A separate cleanup task removes the 10:00 wake entry later, so the client does not have to wait for that extra storage operation. The client can therefore set the 10:05 alarm while the old cleanup is still waiting to run.

After celld confirms that the 10:05 alarm is set, a wake entry must remain that can reactivate the cell by 10:05. The simulator checks that this remains true until the alarm runs or is canceled.

The figure below shows how this invariant is violated when the old cleanup runs after the 10:05 alarm has been set.

In this run, both deleting the 10:00 alarm and setting the new 10:05 alarm returned success while the old cleanup waited. When the simulator finally advanced that cleanup, it removed the 10:00 wake entry that the new alarm still needed. The checker reported an invariant violation: the 10:05 alarm was still set in SQLite, but no wake entry remained to reactivate the cell.

If the node restarted before 10:05, the missing wake entry could prevent the alarm from running, despite the earlier success response.

The simulator found this failing order by exploring requests and pending work. We had not written a test that prescribed this sequence.

We replayed the failure with the same code, settings, and seed. Each run let us inspect the moment the old cleanup deleted the needed wake entry, without searching for the failing order again.

Since then, we have changed the wake-entry design. Each new alarm setting gets its own entry in object storage. A delayed deletion for an older alarm can only remove that older entry, leaving the new one intact. Old entries are removed once celld has confirmed they are no longer needed.

We turned the failing run into a regression test that repeats the requests and cleanup order shown above. It checks that the new alarm keeps a usable wake entry.

The regression test checks the invariant during the run, not just at the end. If the wake entry disappeared and was later restored, checking only the final state would miss the violation.

The simulator is still under development, but it has already helped us find and fix previously unknown bugs in celld. Next, we will test more combinations of requests, storage failures, and node restarts. For example, a node could restart during a storage outage and receive new requests before storage recovers.

We will also add checks for more of celld’s guarantees. A write reported as successful, for example, must survive a node restart. When these tests find a bug, we can replay the failure, fix it, and keep the sequence as a regression test.

items.title: Il tribunale di Roma ha respinto il ricorso con cui Sigfrido Ranucci chiedeva di essere reintegrato alla conduzione di “Report”
items.content:
Il tribunale di Roma ha respinto il ricorso con cui il giornalista Sigfrido Ranucci aveva contestato la decisione della Rai di rimuoverlo dalla conduzione di Report , il più noto programma televisivo di giornalismo d’inchiesta in Italia, trasmesso da Rai 3.

Ranucci era stato rimosso a fine agosto. La decisione aveva a che fare con quanto emerso nelle indagini sull’attentato contro lo stesso Ranucci, compiuto nell’ottobre del 2025 davanti a casa sua e organizzato da Valter Lavitola, imprenditore coinvolto in diversi scandali della politica italiana recente e molto amico di Ranucci (che non è indagato).

Gli avvocati di Ranucci avevano presentato ricorso in via d’urgenza , con l’obiettivo di farlo reintegrare alla conduzione di Report in tempo per l’inizio della nuova stagione, previsto per l’8 novembre. Nel frattempo la Rai ha scelto come nuovi conduttori Claudia Di Pasquale e Daniele Piervincenzi.

Lunedì la Rai aveva sospeso Ranucci per dieci giorni. Secondo diverse ricostruzioni, le ragioni della sospensione sarebbero l’aver inoltrato alcune mail aziendali riservate a Lavitola; la denigrazione dei due colleghi scelti come nuovi conduttori di Report ; l’aver pubblicato i contenuti di una conversazione privata con il deputato del Movimento 5 Stelle Dario Carotenuto; e l’aver fatto entrare nella sede della Rai l’ex sindacalista della CISL Laura Cianfoni.

items.summary: Sono immagini basate esclusivamente sulle indiscrezioni, nulla di ufficiale. Quanto ci sarà andato vicino il leaker?
items.content:
Apple potrebbe presentare a breve il suo primo display intelligente per la casa, insieme a una nuova generazione di dispositivi per l'ecosistema domestico. Come vi abbiamo riportato nelle scorse settimane, il cosiddetto HomePad (nome ancora completamente provvisorio, beninteso) avrà un design ispirato al celebre iMac G4 del 2002; ora possiamo farci un'idea più precisa di cosa potrebbe significare, precisamente, grazie all'ultimo video del leaker Jon Prosser di Front Page Tech.

Nel video ci sono alcuni render del device, che vi proponiamo per comodità anche in questo articolo, ma è importante sottolineare un dettaglio fondamentale: sono creazioni della fonte, o comunque non di Apple o suoi partner, basate unicamente sulle indiscrezioni emerse fino a qui. Non è quindi materiale ufficiale, né derivato da materiale ufficiale (come per esempio possono essere i file CAD nel mondo smartphone).

items.title: Rampart: Browser native on-device PII radaction
items.summary: Article URL: https://ndstudio.gov/posts/say-hello-to-rampart Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50024242 Points: 82 # Comments: 32
items.content:
When you type into a chatbot, you might reveal more about yourself than you intend. A request to clean up an email carries your name and your coworker’s; a question about a medical bill carries your address and account number; a vented frustration carries who you are and where you live. And whatever you type doesn’t stay with you — it travels to a remote server you have no way to inspect.

Our core design principle is that the only personal information you can be sure is private is the information that never leaves your device .

Today, we open source Rampart — a first-generation on-device personal information filtering system that is a strong first line of defense in ensuring your personal information never leaves your device. Rampart is a combination of a deterministic layer, based on regular expressions to catch SSNs and ID numbers, and MiniLM to catch names and street addresses.

Often times, doing PII removal means either trusting a remote server or downloading binaries to the client, which present a few key challenges:

Everything happens in the browser, in the moment between typing a message and sending it; there is no server in the loop.

Before the message goes anywhere, two readers look at it on your device.

The first is a set of rules. Regular expressions paired with real validations handle the information that has structure: Social Security numbers, credit cards, phone numbers, routing and account numbers, emails, IP addresses, government IDs. It is deterministic and fast.

The second is a small language model. Rules can’t anticipate every name or street address, so MiniLM reads the sentence for the personal information with a deeper understanding of the context of the sentence, then redacts information it finds within a specific category.

For example, say you type a sentence full of personal information into chat:

Rampart redacts PII on-device so it doesn’t have to leave your device

The browser stores relevant PII temporarily on your device to fill in the blanks

My name is [GIVEN_NAME] [SURNAME] , my Social Security number is [SSN] , and I make $1,950 a month. Can you help me find affordable housing?

Original: My name is Maria Garcia, my Social Security number is 123-45-6789, and I make $1,950 a month. Can you help me find affordable housing?

After redaction: My name is [GIVEN_NAME] [SURNAME], my Social Security number is [SSN], and I make $1,950 a month. Can you help me find affordable housing?

We trained Rampart on AI4Privacy’s OpenPII 1.5M dataset and a synthetic generator that reinforces all 17 entity types with deliberately messy chat-style input. The headline numbers below come from a 30,000-row held-out OpenPII slice spanning seven Latin-script languages, scored end-to-end by the shipped pipeline.

Private-term recall on a 30,000-row held-out OpenPII test set across seven supported languages. Higher is better. Benchmark ↗ (opens in new tab)

Rampart is an alpha product intended to be the first line of defense in a more thorough effort to manage personally identifiable information for AI chat experiences. It currently supports English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Dutch.

Download the model on HuggingFace, install the NPM library, or read the whitepaper.

items.title: Sony dice addio alla VR? Vende tantissimi brevetti a Meta
items.summary: Oltre 400 brevetti ceduti al colosso americano. PlayStation VR3 non si farà?
items.content:
Esiste la possibilità molto concreta che un PlayStation VR 3 non si farà: a quanto pare Sony ha venduto a Meta un sacco di suoi brevetti sulle tecnologie di realtà virtuale, aumentata e mista. L'hanno scoperto i colleghi di ZDNet consultando documentazione ufficiale degli uffici statunitense e internazionale per la proprietà intellettuale: la società nipponica ha apparentemente ceduto al colosso di Zuckerberg un totale di 419 brevetti, tramite un documento firmato già a dicembre 2025 e chiamato Confirmatory Assignment.

Non sappiamo naturalmente se sono tutti i brevetti che ha depositato Sony in merito, ma il pacchetto comprende invenzioni registrate tra il 2010 e il 2022 riguardo a riguarda visori, occhiali per la realtà estesa e sistemi di tracking dell'utente. 180 brevetti sono registrati negli USA, e 43 di questi sono stati trasferiti a Meta tra giugno e settembre 2026; gli altri 239 sono registrati in Giappone, Cina, Corea del Sud, Europa e altre regioni.

La notizia è un po' sorprendente perché appena un paio d'anni fa Eric Lempel, vicepresidente senior dell'azienda, aveva definito la realtà virtuale un settore importante. Il trasferimento di una quantità di brevetti così ampia nel settore sembra segnalare in modo piuttosto deciso un cambiamento di strategia, anche se è importante precisare che ci sono diversi elementi ancora poco chiari in tutta la vicenda, che chiaramente le due aziende intendono tenere segreta al di là di ciò che è strettamente necessario divulgare per questioin legali / burocratiche.

items.title: Da Palazzo Piacentini alla Villa La Tesoriera, tornano le giornate Fai d'Autunno
items.summary: Oltre 700 luoghi aperti in 350 città il 10 e 11 ottobre per la 15/a edizione
items.content:
L'imponenza dell'arte che sfida il tempo tra i marmi di Palazzo Piacentini a Roma, accesi dai colori della maestosa vetrata di Mario Sironi, o la grazia barocca di Villa La Tesoriera a Torino, immersa nel silenzio del suo parco. Le memorie della diplomazia e del collezionismo custodite a Villa Giorgina, fino al genio senza tempo di Francesco Borromini a Palazzo Carpegna. Ma anche la meraviglia del patrimonio ritrovato a Milano con la riapertura straordinaria di Palazzo Dugnani e le sue volte affrescate da Tiepolo, la solennità medievale di Palazzo Sclafani a Palermo con le sue tracce arabo-normanne, la raffinatezza rinascimentale di Palazzo Gualfonda a Firenze e l'emozione di varcare per la prima volta le porte di Palazzo Saladini Pilastri ad Ascoli Piceno con la sua chiesa inglobata.

È con questo sguardo emozionante e profondo sulle grandi architetture d'Italia che sabato 10 e domenica 11 ottobre tornano le Giornate Fai d'Autunno, la grande manifestazione di piazza del Fondo per l'Ambiente Italiano giunta alla 15/a edizione. In 350 città italiane apriranno eccezionalmente oltre 700 luoghi straordinari, molti dei quali solitamente inaccessibili, con un'attenzione speciale riservata quest'anno all'artigianato e al Made in Italy attraverso 75 visite dedicate.

A fare gli onori di casa durante la presentazione a Palazzo Piacentini è stato il ministro delle Imprese e del Made in Italy, Adolfo Urso: "Credo che questa iniziativa del Fai sia di estrema importanza, soprattutto in questo momento, perché valorizza quello che è un patrimonio del nostro Paese, quindi la sua cultura produttiva fatta di marchi che si sono fatti largo nel mondo. È un sistema di eccellenza e di qualità che ci consente di crescere nei momenti di crisi globale".

Un concetto ribadito dal presidente del Fai, Marco Magnifico: "I monumenti raccontano il passato, le imprese artigiane e le piccole imprese raccontano il presente e il futuro. Si protegge ciò che si ama, ma si ama ciò che si conosce".

Sull'importanza dell'iniziativa è intervenuto anche Francesco Somma, vicepresidente per la Cultura d'Impresa di Confindustria, sottolineando come "il patrimonio industriale sia un pezzo importante del patrimonio della cultura italiana".

Stefano Coletta, direttore del Coordinamento Generi Rai, ha ricordato la partnership che dura "da più di 10 anni": "La divulgazione della bellezza, soprattutto nei siti dei beni culturali, è memoria, è presente ma è anche futuro", ha evidenziato, annunciando che dal 5 all'11 ottobre "tutta l'offerta televisiva, radiofonica e quella digitale di RaiPlay Sound dedicheranno tanti spazi ai siti e a tutte le iniziative che il Fai realizza in questi giorni, in piena coerenza con la divulgazione del territorio che la Rai realizza in tutta la sua programmazione".

items.title: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
items.summary: Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the tech firm admits customers may experience disruption to digital services due to the attacks.
items.content:
Russian tech giant Yandex has said it was struggling to maintain services after two of its five data centres were struck by Ukrainian drones in the past two days.

Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the company runs the country's most popular search engine, as well as a food-ordering and taxi app used by tens of millions of people.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks were in response to weeks of Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centres.

Both sides have stepped up attacks on infrastructure in recent months as the war between the two drags on. Kyiv says its strikes are aimed at revenue streams for Moscow's war machine, and that the latest attacks could force Russia to divert resources to Yandex.

Yandex said that its data centre in Sasovo, in the Ryazan region, had been "seriously damaged as a result of a drone attack" overnight into Thursday, with its operations "completely suspended".

Another data centre in Kaluga, a region south-west of Moscow, had also been attacked on Friday morning, it said, with part of that site's infrastructure "taken out of service".

Yandex said on Friday that its data centres were "critical" for the normal operation of its services and that it was "very difficult to predict" when they would be back online.

It said teams were working "day and night" to keep services running, but "unfortunately it is not a simple task".

The tech giant said none of its employees had been injured in the strikes. The regional governor in Kaluga said nine people had been injured in a drone attack on the city's infrastructure.

The exact scope of the disruption to the company's services is unclear - though it told state news agency Tass that some of its AI chatbot functions were temporarily unavailable, while its smart home devices may also experience problems.

Yandex previously said its Kaluga data centre was one of Russia's largest - covering an area of 130,000 sqm (1,399,000 sq ft) and consuming as much electricity annually as 220,000 UK households.

Its data centre in Sasovo, meanwhile, houses two of three supercomputers used to develop the company's AI model. It is unclear whether the supercomputers survived the attack.

Ukraine's defence ministry confirmed the data centre attacks, saying they could "force Russia to divert resources to repair the damaged capacity".

Zelensky said Kyiv was responding to similar Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centres in a "mirror-like fashion".

Last month, a Russian drone hit a business centre in Kyiv , killing four people and damaging a data centre. Due to the strikes, about 100,000 households in Kyiv and the region suffered internet outages.

Some Ukrainian firms have already begun moving data from damaged servers to facilities abroad.

Moscow has justified the attacks by saying the data centres were used by Ukrainian military intelligence.

But Ukraine accuses it of deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure. Russia has stepped up strikes on energy infrastructure ahead of the winter, as it has done in previous years of the full-scale invasion, which began in 2022.

Russia targeting 'ordinary life' with attacks on Ukraine's data centres, Zelensky says

Russian strikes and approaching winter force some in Kyiv to pack bags and flee

Russian strike on buses kills at least 30, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge

Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 22 in block of flats

items.title: L’ex sindaca di Prato Ilaria Bugetti è stata rinviata a giudizio per corruzione
items.summary: Si era dimessa a giugno del 2025 proprio dopo aver saputo di essere indagata
items.content:
L’ex sindaca di Prato Ilaria Bugetti, del Partito Democratico, è stata rinviata a giudizio con l’accusa di corruzione: si era dimessa a giugno del 2025 proprio a causa delle indagini nei suoi confronti. È accusata di aver ricevuto soldi e voti in cambio di favori a Riccardo Matteini Bresci, un imprenditore del tessile con incarichi in Confindustria, la principale organizzazione che rappresenta le imprese italiane. È stato rinviato a giudizio anche Matteini Bresci.

Bugetti aveva deciso di dimettersi qualche giorno dopo che l’inchiesta nei suoi confronti era diventata di pubblico dominio, per via delle pressioni del suo partito. Era diventata sindaca di Prato nel 2024, quando fu eletta col sostegno del centrosinistra e del Movimento 5 Stelle. Prima era stata per due mandati consigliera regionale del PD. La vicenda è rilevante perché riguarda Prato, sede del distretto tessile più grande d’Europa , e le accuse di corruzione nei confronti di una sindaca che avrebbe favorito un imprenditore del settore.

Secondo l’accusa Bugetti si sarebbe spesa in più occasioni per aiutare Matteini Bresci, con cui aveva un rapporto professionale molto stretto. In particolare sarebbe intervenuta per risolvere alcuni problemi legati alla depurazione delle acque del Gruppo Colle, di cui Matteini Bresci era amministratore, garantendo risparmi all’azienda. Durante la campagna elettorale del 2024 avrebbe inoltre sollecitato tariffe di depurazione più basse e promosso una rete fognaria industriale, evitando al Gruppo Colle di costruire un costoso impianto in autonomia.

Altre accuse riguardano il periodo in cui era in consiglio regionale: la procura sostiene che Bugetti abbia fatto da tramite con gli uffici regionali per correggere un decreto che fissava i limiti di prelievo dell’acqua per alimentare una centrale idroelettrica della Hydro Green Energy, società di cui era vicepresidente Matteini Bresci. Sempre durante il mandato da consigliera regionale, Bugetti avrebbe chiesto agli uffici regionali di alzare i limiti previsti per lo scarico delle acque reflue industriali nella rete fognaria.

In cambio di questi favori Bugetti sarebbe stata assunta da Broker Techno, azienda controllata da una società a sua volta partecipata da altre due società riconducibili a Matteini Bresci. Il contratto, concluso nel 2024, avrebbe garantito a Bugetti circa 48mila euro senza fare sostanzialmente nessun lavoro. Bugetti avrebbe inoltre omesso di dichiarare l’incarico agli uffici amministrativi della Regione Toscana. Matteini Bresci avrebbe poi contribuito a finanziare la campagna elettorale di Bugetti con 27mila euro, una parte consistente dei 133mila raccolti dall’allora candidata del centrosinistra.

Insieme a Bugetti e Matteini Bresci sono state rinviate a giudizio altre due persone: Enrico Cini, titolare della Broker Techno, accusato di truffa ai danni dello stato per aver fatto ottenere indebitamente a Bugetti poco più di 300 euro di cassa integrazione durante la pandemia; e Alessio Bitozzi del Consorzio Progetto Acqua, accusato di aver fatto da intermediario tra Matteini Bresci e il Comune per ottenere la concessione dell’area di un ex campo sportivo.

items.title: Man named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
items.summary: The left-wing candidate won a narrow victory in a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, exit polls show.
items.content:
A man named Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores has secured a narrow victory in Peru's local elections, exit polls show.

The candidate for the centre-left Ahora Nación party was elected mayor of Queropalca, a remote district in the Peruvian Andes.

Some 229 residents voted for the 45-year-old, putting him ahead of the second-place candidate from right-wing Renovación Popular Perú by just 25 votes.

Despite being elected to represent fewer than 1,000 people, his forenames being those of two notorious fascist dictators has drawn outsized international attention to the small corner of the country.

Data from Peru's elections office showed a little over 700 people had participated in the election, with Simeon securing around 34% of the vote.

He was born in the district in the central department of Huánuco, some 360km (224 miles) from the capital, Lima, according to his candidate profile.

That he shares his name with Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini - "two of the most well-known figures of 20th-Century European totalitarian regimes" - has made his candidacy a "striking event", local outlet Peru21 reported.

Despite the curiosity generated by his name, local media noted that Hitler Guesclin Alba Sánchez had been elected mayor of Yúngar in 2018.

He reportedly beat rival candidate Lenin Vladimir Rodríguez Valverde after campaigning on the slogan "I'm the good Hitler".

A politician named Adolf Hitler Uunona attracted similar attention in 2020 after winning local elections in Namibia - a former German colony where Adolf and other Germanic first names are not uncommon.

items.title: Il Tesla Full Self Driving diventa Tesla Assisted Driving e si avvia all’approvazione in tutta l’Unione Europea
items.summary: Il ministero dei trasporti tedesco aveva avvisato Tesla che non avrebbe mai approvato il sistema di guida autonoma di livello 2 con il nome attuale perché giudicato fuorviante. Ora Tesla si è adeguata ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
La Germania è uno degli stati essenziali per l’approvazione a livello europeo del sistema di assistenza alla guida di Tesla Full Self Driving (Supervised), il cui voto è atteso tra un paio di mesi. In settimana, il Ministro dei Trasporti tedesco Steffen Bilger si è detto più che favorevole a farsi portavoce di un celere adeguamento della normativa europea al fine di consentire il lancio del sistema in Germania e in Europa, ma ad una condizione: Tesla deve cambiare nome.

Bilger, in una nota rilasciata sul sito del ministero, ha infatti sottolineato come il nome Full Self Driving sia ingannevole in quanto all’atto pratico il sistema di Tesla al momento non esonera il guidatore dal mantenere l’attenzione sulla strada: “ il nome attuale "FSD" è un po' fuorviante. Non si tratta di un sistema che si assume l'intero compito di guida. In effetti, si tratta di un sistema di assistenza alla guida che può supportare determinate attività di guida come l'accelerazione, la frenata e lo sterzo. Tuttavia, l'autista deve rimanere sempre attento ”.

In seguito al rispetto dell’accordo, il ministro tedesco ha dichiarato che “ su questa base, mi impegnerò ora affinché il sistema sia approvato tempestivamente in tutta Europa. Il mio obiettivo è che i conducenti di Tesla possano sfruttare al più presto i vantaggi della guida assistita in tutta l’UE ”.

Il lancio della a lungo attesa funzionalità in Europa potrebbe quindi essere ormai davvero prossimo.

items.title: Il lago di Garda ora ha un anello in fibra ottica lungo 155 chilometri. Lo ha realizzato Mynet
items.summary: Mynet ha chiuso la rete interrata tra Verona, Brescia e Trento dopo dieci anni di lavori. Un anello in fibra che ha il vantaggio di non fermare il traffico in caso di guasti sulla linea ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Dopo dieci anni di cantieri l’operatore mantovano Mynet ha completato l’anello in fibra ottica attorno al lago di Garda: circa 155 chilometri di rete interrata che attraversano i comuni rivieraschi delle province di Verona, Brescia e Trento, e rendono Mynet l’unico operatore in grado di offrire una copertura ad anello lungo tutte le sponde del lago.

Il progetto era nato con ambizioni più contenute, perché in origine si trattava di collegare le utenze della costa veronese e di quella bresciana, formate in gran parte alberghi e strutture ricettive. I lavori sono partiti dalla sponda orientale, tra Peschiera del Garda, Lazise e Bardolino, e sono poi risaliti verso Garda, Torri del Benaco, Brenzone e Malcesine. A chiudere il percorso sono stati gli ultimi sei chilometri di scavo tra la galleria nord di Malcesine e Nago-Torbole, già in Trentino.

Una rete chiusa su se stessa, come quella ad anello, ha un vantaggio pratico, perché ogni Comune risulta raggiungibile da due direzioni: se per esempio uno scavo trancia il cavo tra Malcesine e Torbole, il traffico può fare il giro dall’altra sponda del lago invece di interrompersi.

Per limitare gli scavi Mynet ha stipulato convenzioni con i Comuni e ha sfruttato infrastrutture pubbliche già presenti, come l’illuminazione delle ciclovie . Le stesse amministrazioni potranno appoggiarsi alla fibra per la videosorveglianza, il Wi-Fi pubblico o il controllo a distanza dei varchi.

Il direttore generale di Mynet, Giovanni Zorzoni, ha definito l’anello “lo sforzo più significativo” compiuto dall’azienda sul Garda, frutto anche di lunghe trattative con i singoli Comuni.

Considerando la zona, il bacino di utenza più rilevante resta comunque quello turistico. Un riferimento abbastanza recente: il lago di Garda nel 2025 ha registrato il record di circa 28 milioni di presenze.
